the sequence attributes of cysteine, aromatic, charge, flexible and hydrophobic are the best attributes for discriminating between ordered and disordered proteins.
the Sequence Attribute Method can be used to rank the ability of sequence attributes to predict order or disorder in proteins.

the application of Bayesian probability theory to the problem of predicting protein disorder.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single attribute that can be used to predict protein disorder, but that the best combination of attributes will be those that are sensitive to local sequence context.
there is a strong relationship between the disorder and the attributes of cysteine, aromatic, flexible, and charge, and that there are no other attributes with a comparable relationship to disorder.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a significant correlation between disorder and the presence of flexible, charged, and aromatic residues, and between order and the presence of cysteine residues.
the best sequence attributes for distinguishing order from disorder are those that describe local flexibility and charge.
the best attributes for predicting disorder in proteins are the cysteine content and the flexible and aromatic content, with the aromatic content being slightly more effective.

the sequence attribute method is a powerful and flexible tool for determining relationships between sequence and protein disorder and for quantifying these relationships.
